title: RAG corpus list
description: The repos a RAG provider ingests. The provider follows each entry's branch head and every chunk names the commit it came from; nothing is pinned (mcl-rag#24). Ids must also be unique in the list, which JSON Schema cannot state; mcl-rag refuses a duplicate (duplicate_id).

id.description: Names the checkout directory and the ingest namespace (<id>/<path>). Renaming an entry re-ingests it.

url.description: An https clone url, or an absolute path to a git repo on the provider's own box. No credentials are ever used.

branch.description: The branch whose head is followed.

depth.description: Bound the fetch of this repo's first clone to this many commits (a shallow checkout, so it holds far less history; 1 is usually all the refresh reads). Absent or 0 fetches the full history. It applies at the first clone only: a checkout that already exists full is not converted (delete it to have it re-cloned), a shallow one stays shallow and its later fetches bring only new commits.

paths.description: Materialise and ingest only these repo-root-relative prefixes; the ingest walker reads nothing outside them, and files outside them that an earlier full checkout left on disk are not touched, pruned or read. Absent means the whole tree. This bounds the working tree; the fetch still brings the branch's objects, so bound the download with depth.

items.description: A file or directory prefix, like `docs' or `Documentation/guides'; a trailing slash is ignored. Letters, digits and . _ - / beyond the first character, and no `..' segment.
